subject: Onboarding: cost & performance tuning plan

Subject: Re: Initial onboarding discussion - cost & perf tuning

Ben — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Finovexa is excited to move to the pilot. Before we lock dates, team leadership asked for a short plan that explains how Redwood will help us get to acceptable latency and predictable cost once we flip traffic. Can you outline the onboarding activities that specifically address:

- Batching & queueing strategy for our 1–3s interactive flows
- Caching and prefix-KV reuse for common prompts
- Recommended quantization profiles (we run on T4s in staging)
- Routing fallbacks (cheaper models vs. low-latency SLA paths)

We have a procurement touchpoint (Michael) who will need a rough timeline and any immediate blockers for procurement (e.g., network peering, SOC2 evidence). Happy to take a short plan, or schedule a 30m to walk through.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of ML Engineering
Finovexa

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding discussion - cost & perf tuning

Hi Priya — great to hear. I've sketched a 2-week pilot plan below (high level), and copied Marissa (CS, cost/perf lead) and Tessa (solutions) to join the technical call. If this looks good we can lock a recurring 30m cadence during onboarding.

Proposed 2-week onboarding sprint (pilot-focused):
1) Kickoff + telemetry handoff (Day 0–1)
   - Map production-like traces (sample traffic) and SLAs
   - Share access checklist (VPC peering, API keys, sample prompts)

2) Baseline run + quick wins (Day 2–4)
   - Run baseline with current model selection and measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost/token
   - Enable prefix KV caching for top 20% prompts

3) Batching & quantization experiments (Day 5–10)
   - Evaluate batching window (5–15ms) for interactive paths, measure tail latency impact
   - Try quant profiles: int8 fast vs. int4 cost-optimized; compare quality with eval set

4) Routing & rollout policy (Day 10–12)
   - Define routing policy: latency-first for checkout flows, cost-first for background jobs
   - Set canary rollout for any model changes with automatic fallback

5) Handoff + runbook (Day 13–14)
   - Deliver runbook: thresholds, recommended cache hit rates, and quant profile mappings

I've attached a short MVP proposal detailing batching and a sample quantization matrix. Marissa — can you add the evaluation checklist (prompt-set, pass/fail)?

Next step: propose 11/09 or 11/10 10am PT for a 30m technical kickoff.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success (Pilot Programs)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mvp-batching-proposal.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial onboarding discussion - cost & perf tuning

Thanks Ben — adding technical detail and an eval checklist below so Priya's team knows acceptance criteria up front. Quick notes:

Baseline metrics to collect (samples):
- P50 / P95 / P99 latency for sample flows (cold and warm KV)
- Tokens per second and mean active batch size
- Cache hit rate per prompt bucket (we'll ask for top 200 prompts)

Eval checklist (pass/fail items):
- Quality regression <= 2% on the sample prompt set after quantization
- Tail latency p95 within 20% of baseline for interactive flows with batching enabled
- Cost reduction >= 25% per token for background async flows after routing to cost tier

Quantization guidance (initial):
- Staging (T4): try dynamic int8 with per-channel quant for LLM-11B variant; if quality drop observed, fall back to int8 symmetric
- If model supports, test int4-optimized profile on a 2-hour window for low-priority workloads

Batching heuristics:
- Interactive: target batch size 4–8, batch window 8–12ms (tune to p95 requirement)
- Async: larger window (50–150ms), target batch >= 32

Routing policy examples:
- Route by route label: route=checkout -> latency tier (single model pinned, no quant)
- route=analytics -> cost tier (quantized model, aggressive batching)

I'll collect a short prompt set request and send the link. Connor, can you prepare the staging runbook and the sample quant-profiles.csv?

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference

Following up with a concrete staging implementation checklist and timeline that matches Marissa's eval work:

Implementation checklist (staging):
- [ ] Provide sample traces + top 200 prompts (Priya)
- [ ] Grant staging API key and optional VPC peering creds (Finovexa infra)
- [ ] Deploy baseline model and collect 24h of metrics
- [ ] Apply prefix-KV caching for top prompt buckets
- [ ] Run batching experiments with the first two batch-window settings (8ms, 12ms)
- [ ] Run quantization candidates (int8 dyn, int4 opt) against eval set and capture quality scores
- [ ] Configure routing policies and create a canary route for checkout flow
- [ ] Produce runbook and rollback steps

Timeline (working days):
- Day 0: Kickoff + access
- Day 1–2: Baseline collection
- Day 3–6: Batching + cache experiments
- Day 7–9: Quantization experiments + QA
- Day 10: Routing config + canary rollout
- Day 11: Deliver runbook and handoff

Attachments: quant-profiles.csv (contains candidate profiles and quick notes).

I'll set up a shared folder and a short test harness script (curl + sample prompts) so your infra team can run local smoke checks before we flip traffic. Suggested kickoff: 11/09 10am PT or 11/10 10am PT.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
